title: Stack every objective in the area
advice: Work every kill and loot objective in this area in one sweep; kill the other quests' mobs as they come.
rationale: Travel, not killing, is most of a leveling hour: one pass through a camp that advances 3 quests saves a return trip per quest (typically 1-3 min each). RestedXP encodes this with #completewith steps.

title: Kill what blocks the path, never detour
advice: Kill this mob only if it's in your path; don't step off the line for it.
rationale: A same-level mob is 5*level+45 XP (95 at 10, 145 at 20) for ~15-25 s of fighting, but a detour adds walking and downtime; a mob in your path would also daze you from behind if you ran past it.

title: Turn in everything at the hub in one visit
advice: Hand in every completed quest here and take every follow-up before you leave the hub.
rationale: Each extra visit to a hub costs the round trip; RestedXP groups turn-ins so one stop clears the log and re-fills it with the next loop's quests.

title: Take every guide quest before leaving
advice: Grab every quest this hub offers that the guide lists before you run out; coming back for one costs minutes.
rationale: Quest givers in a hub are seconds apart, while the objectives are minutes away; a missed pickup means a second round trip or a skipped quest worth roughly a full level-appropriate turn-in.

title: Above the guide's range: cut extras
advice: You're above this section's level range: skip optional and low-XP steps and get to the next zone.
rationale: Quests drop to 80% XP at 6 levels above their level and to 10% at 10+; mobs 5+ levels below give half XP or less (1-diff/ZD). Staying in an outleveled zone lowers XP per minute.

title: Below the guide's range: close the gap first
advice: You're 2+ levels under this section: grind at-level mobs on the way or finish the previous zone first.
rationale: Quests 3+ levels above you are orange/red: slower kills, more misses and resists, more deaths. RestedXP sets XP gates (.xp steps) for exactly this reason.

title: Grind exactly to the XP gate
advice: Grind to the number the step shows on the closest dense mobs, then stop and move on.
rationale: RestedXP grind steps (.xp level+XP) exist because the next quests need that level; XP beyond the gate is earned at grind rate, usually below quest rate, so overshooting wastes time.

title: Grind mobs at your level to +2
advice: Pick mobs from your level to 2 above that die fast; skip low greens and anything elite.
rationale: Kill XP = (5*level+45) * (1 + 0.05*levels above, max +4) and * (1 - levels below/ZD) for lower mobs. A +2 mob is +10% XP but takes noticeably longer; a mob 5 below at level 30 (ZD 12) gives 58%.

title: Grind where the next step starts
advice: Do the grind on mobs next to the next quest giver or turn-in so the last kill puts you at the NPC.
rationale: Grinding far from the next step adds a walk after the gate; RestedXP places grinds on the way for this reason.

title: Abandon a dry collection quest
advice: If 25 or more kills haven't finished the drops, skip it and move on; come back only if it's on the route.
rationale: Low drop rates turn a 5-minute objective into 15+; RestedXP's notes on low-drop quests say to skip after 25+ kills without a drop. Your XP/min on a dry collection quest is roughly kill XP only.

title: Check you're killing the right mob
advice: Re-read the objective: confirm which mob drops the item before killing more of these.
rationale: Neighbouring camps often hold similar mobs (e.g. Kobold Workers vs Laborers, Defias Thugs) and only one drops the item; on 2026-10-04 the player lost minutes on the wrong mob for Red Burlap Bandanas.

title: Escorts: go only if the NPC is there
advice: Start the escort only if the NPC is standing there; if someone else is running it, skip or come back later.
rationale: Escorts are walk-speed, often spawn ambushes and fail if the NPC dies; waiting for a reset can take several minutes. RestedXP marks hard escorts as optional.

title: Skip far single turn-ins
advice: A lone turn-in more than ~2 minutes off the route is only worth it if it unlocks a follow-up chain.
rationale: A 2-minute detour each way costs about as much XP as one full-value quest pays at your pace (4 minutes at 21k XP/hour is 1,400 XP); it's a gain only when the turn-in pays more than that or unlocks follow-ups on the route.

title: Breadcrumbs only if they're on the way
advice: Breadcrumb quests (talk to someone elsewhere) are free XP only when that NPC is on your route anyway.
rationale: Breadcrumbs pay small XP and exist to point you at a hub; if the guide already sends you there, take it, otherwise it's a detour.

title: Judge a quest by its chain
advice: A low-XP opener is worth it when its follow-ups are on your route; judge the chain's total XP per minute.
rationale: Chains often end in the biggest reward (XP and an item) and later parts reuse the same area; RestedXP keeps openers like a 85 XP pickup that unlocks a 170 XP kill quest in the same camp.

title: Behind pace: drop optional steps
advice: This step is optional and you're behind pace: skip it.
rationale: RestedXP marks steps optional when they're marginal (rare spawn, limited vendor item, small reward). When XP/hour is under 80% of benchmark, marginal steps are the first to cut.

title: Step pays less than your pace
advice: This step earns under half your current XP rate; skip it unless it unlocks the next quests.
rationale: Every minute spent on a step yields step_xp_per_min; when that is below half of your rolling XP/min, doing it lowers the hour's total unless a later step depends on it.

title: Stuck: name the cause, then fix or skip
advice: You've been on this step a while: check for the wrong mob, competition for spawns, or a missing item; fix it or skip it now.
rationale: Most stalls come from three things: the wrong drop source, other players camping the spawn, or a respawn timer (~5 min on most open-world mobs). A stall past 5 minutes rarely recovers by waiting.

title: Moving away from the waypoint
advice: You're heading away from the step's waypoint; turn back unless you're deliberately clearing a stacked objective.
rationale: Off-route movement is the most common silent time loss; a wrong turn of 30 s costs a minute round trip.

title: The guide's order is deliberate
advice: Follow the guide's order unless you have a concrete reason: it already accounts for respawns, gates and travel.
rationale: RestedXP routes are tuned from many runs: steps are ordered so quests complete on the way, hearths line up with cooldowns and XP gates are met. Reordering by feel usually adds a trip.

title: Complete-with steps run in the background
advice: Do this objective while you follow the next steps; don't stop to finish it now.
rationale: #completewith in RestedXP means the step's objective is collected opportunistically until the labelled later step; finishing it early wastes time on mobs you'd meet anyway.

title: Sticky step: keep it in mind
advice: This objective stays active across the next steps; tag its mobs or items whenever they're near.
rationale: #sticky steps stay on screen until complete; they're objectives scattered over the zone (e.g. drops from many mob types) that the route covers incidentally.

title: Quest log nearly full
advice: Your log is nearly full: abandon the lowest-value quest that isn't on the route before you need the slot.
rationale: Classic caps the quest log at 20; a full log means a quest giver's offer is lost or you stop to abandon mid-hub.

title: Quest log full
advice: Log is full and this step accepts a quest: abandon a gray or off-route quest first.
rationale: With 20 quests (Classic cap) you cannot accept anything; deciding now is faster than doing it at the NPC.

title: Abandon quests 10+ levels under you
advice: A quest 10+ levels below you pays only 10% XP: abandon it unless its turn-in is on your route.
rationale: Quest XP is full up to quest level +5, then 80/60/40/20% at +6/+7/+8/+9 and 10% from +10.

title: Turn in before you out-level it
advice: Turn in your completed low quest before your next ding or two; at 6 levels over it starts losing XP.
rationale: Full quest XP holds up to quest level +5; at +6 you get 80%, +7 60%, +8 40%, +9 20%, +10 10%. A 1,000 XP quest turned in 2 levels late loses 400 XP.

title: Decayed turn-ins: on the way only
advice: This completed quest already lost XP to your level; turn it in only if its NPC is on the route.
rationale: At +6..+9 levels a turn-in pays 80/60/40/20% of its value; a detour to collect 20-40% is rarely worth the walk.

title: Make the ding happen at the trainer
advice: These turn-ins level you to an even level: do them in the town with your class trainer and train right away.
rationale: Classic class trainers add spells at even levels; dinging in a trainer town saves a separate trip to train the new rank.

title: Keep quests the guide says to hold
advice: Hold this completed quest as the guide says; it's being saved for a later XP gate or a combined turn-in.
rationale: RestedXP sometimes delays turn-ins so their XP lands where a level is required (next zone's quests, class training) or to turn in several at one NPC.

title: Do pre-quests that open big chains
advice: Do a low-XP pre-quest when it opens a chain the guide follows; skipping it locks the follow-ups out.
rationale: Prerequisite quests gate follow-ups (quest_prereq); the follow-ups are usually worth far more than the pre-quest costs.

title: Elite quest at your level: group or skip
advice: This is an elite/group quest at your level: find a group in a couple of minutes or skip it.
rationale: Elite mobs have roughly 2-3x the health and damage of normals; solo attempts within 2 levels mostly end in a death (corpse run plus sickness at 11+).

title: Ask for a group while you quest nearby
advice: Post in /1 for this group quest while you finish nearby objectives; if nobody joins in ~5 minutes, skip it.
rationale: Waiting idle for a group is pure loss; overlapping the search with nearby solo objectives keeps XP flowing.

title: Class quests on the route are worth it
advice: Do this class quest: class quests give spells, forms or items you'd otherwise miss.
rationale: Class quests (Bear Form, Voidwalker, totems, pet taming, poisons) are core power spikes; RestedXP routes them where they cost the least.

title: Collect every dungeon quest before entering
advice: Before entering, pick up every quest for this dungeon on your route; the run pays mostly through its quests.
rationale: Dungeon quests are the main XP of a run (on Forever even more: dungeon quest XP was raised and mob kill XP cut).

title: Crowded spawns: group up and share tags
advice: If others are fighting for these spawns, invite them: grouped players all get credit for kill objectives.
rationale: In Classic, party members near a kill share quest kill credit, so a 3-person group finishes a contested kill quest about as fast as an empty camp. Launch day (2026-11-04) starting zones will be packed.

title: Named mob not up: skip
advice: If the named mob isn't up, skip this step; long respawns cost more than the quest pays.
rationale: RestedXP notes long respawn timers on named quest mobs and tells you to skip when they're down.

title: Limited-supply item gone: skip
advice: If the vendor is out of the limited-supply item, skip the step; don't wait for the restock.
rationale: Limited-supply vendor items restock on a timer that can be many minutes; RestedXP marks these steps skippable.

title: Kite tough quest mobs to guards
advice: If this fight is going badly, drag it to the nearest guards, but keep doing damage: you need over half of it for credit.
rationale: Guards will kill a mob that follows you; RestedXP suggests kiting tough mobs to outposts and notes you must deal 50%+ of the damage to get quest credit.

title: Explore objectives only on the path
advice: Walk into the area just far enough for the discovery; exploration XP is small, so don't wander.
rationale: Discovery XP is a few hundred at most at mid levels; it's included in RestedXP only when the area is on the route or a quest needs it.

title: New zone: flight path and bind
advice: New zone: grab the flight path if you pass the flight master and set your hearth only where the guide says.
rationale: A flight path picked up in passing saves a run later; binding at the wrong inn breaks the guide's planned hearth.

title: Waiting for a boat: craft
advice: While you wait for the boat, make bandages or cook; the wait is free crafting time.
rationale: Boats and zeppelins dock for 60 s and cycle every 3-5 minutes; RestedXP tells you to level First Aid and Cooking while waiting for the boat or tram.

title: Use the guide's logout skips
advice: Stand exactly where the guide says and log out and back in; you'll reappear outside, skipping the walk.
rationale: A logout at certain spots inside caves or on objects makes the server place you at a safe outside position; RestedXP marks working spots (e.g. out of caves, Thelsamar tunnel). Elsewhere it does nothing.

title: Log out in rested areas
advice: Log out here: in an inn or capital the logout is instant and rested XP builds 4x faster.
rationale: Outside rested areas logout takes 20 s; inside, it's instant and rest accrues at 5% of a level per 8 h instead of a quarter of that.

title: Bind at the hub you'll return to
advice: Set your hearth here: this is the hub the guide brings you back to with a full log of turn-ins.
rationale: A hearth (10 s cast) replaces a multi-minute run back; binding where the next loop ends converts the cooldown into the biggest single travel saving of the hour.

title: Hearth at the end of the loop
advice: Hearth now: the loop is done and your turn-ins are at your bind point.
rationale: Walking back from the far end of a loop typically costs 3-6 minutes; the hearthstone costs 10 s and its 60-minute cooldown is planned by the guide.

title: Hearth step but stone on cooldown
advice: Hearth isn't ready: grind or finish nearby objectives until it's up instead of walking, unless the walk is shorter than the wait.
rationale: RestedXP itself plans this ("kill worgens until your Hearthstone cooldown is <25 minutes", "grind until your hearth has <2 minutes left"): XP while waiting beats an equal-length walk.

title: Hearthstone cooldown is 60 minutes on Forever
advice: Your hearth is back in 60 minutes; plan the next one at least an hour out.
rationale: Classic hearthstone: 10 s cast, 60 min cooldown. Our recorder read 3598 s of cooldown right after a hearth on the Forever beta (2026-10-04), so Forever keeps the Classic hour.
source: obs:data/live/20261004-154307.jsonl (hearthstone cooldown read 3598 s right after a cast, level 11)

title: Take breaks right after hearthing
advice: If you need a break, take it now, logged out in this inn: the hearth cooldown runs while you're away and you earn rested XP.
rationale: Item cooldowns tick in real time while offline, and an inn logout accrues rest 4x faster than in the world.

title: Don't burn the hearth on a short walk
advice: Don't hearth for a trip under ~2 minutes if the guide needs the stone again within the hour.
rationale: The stone only works once per 60 minutes; spending it on a short walk forces a much longer walk later.

title: Hearth batching (Classic trick)
advice: Hearth batch only if you've practised it: open the bind dialog, start the hearth and confirm the bind as the cast ends.
rationale: On Classic Era servers spell batching lets you bind a new inn and still teleport to the old one; RestedXP uses it (Auberdine to Ironforge). Forever runs a modern server, so whether batching still works is unverified.
source: rxp-guide-text:RestedXP ADV AoE Alliance Mage/10-12 ADV Darkshore 1 Mage AoE

title: Bind changed
advice: Hearth set; your next hearth returns here, so plan the following loop to end near this inn.
rationale: The bind point decides where every later hearth lands; confirm it matches the guide's next .hs step.

title: Mage teleports are a second hearth
advice: Teleport to your capital instead of hearthing when the city is the destination; keep the hearth for the next loop.
rationale: Mages learn Teleport to their faction's capitals at 20 (one more at 30); each costs a Rune of Teleportation and has no hour-long cooldown.

title: Hearth down? Die to the graveyard town
advice: With the hearth on cooldown, the planned deathskip is your fast trip; die near the graveyard you want.
rationale: Spirit resurrection puts you at the nearest graveyard; below level 11 there's no resurrection sickness, so dying is a free teleport.

title: Always take a flight path you pass
advice: Talk to the flight master now; picking up the path costs seconds and saves a run later.
rationale: Flights need both ends discovered; a missing node later forces a long run. RestedXP routes every .fp pickup.

title: Fly long legs, plan during the flight
advice: Take the flight; use the flight time to check the next steps and your bags.
rationale: Taxis are faster than running for long legs and are hands-off; planning in the air avoids stops on the ground.

title: On a flight: prepare the landing
advice: While flying, plan the landing: who to talk to first, what to sell, whether to train.
rationale: Flight time is dead time for movement but not for decisions; arriving with a plan avoids idle seconds at each NPC.

title: Boats run every 3-5 minutes
advice: If the boat just left, use the wait: First Aid, cooking, mail or vendor nearby; it's back within ~5 minutes.
rationale: Boats and zeppelins stay docked 60 s and most routes cycle in 3-5 minutes (e.g. Undercity-Orgrimmar every 3:59).

title: Mount for any real run
advice: Mount up for any run longer than ~20 seconds.
rationale: The Classic riding mount is +60% speed (7 to 11.2 yd/s), so a 20 s run becomes 12.5 s; the 3 s summon pays off beyond that.

title: Mounted daze
advice: Don't ride past mobs that can reach you: a hit from behind can daze and dismount you.
rationale: Any melee hit on a target facing away has a daze chance (20% at equal level, up to 40%, lower under level 30): 4 s at -50% speed and a forced dismount.

title: Shaman: Ghost Wolf for travel
advice: Use Ghost Wolf for runs until you have a mount.
rationale: Ghost Wolf (level 20) is +40% run speed outdoors; it has a cast time and can be dazed, so start it out of reach of mobs.

title: Druid: Travel Form
advice: Travel Form for every outdoor run; it's instant and nearly as fast as a mount.
rationale: Travel Form (level 30) gives +40% outdoor speed (a mount is +60%) with no reagent; shifting also breaks snares.

title: Hunter: Aspect of the Cheetah
advice: Run with Aspect of the Cheetah, but switch off it before you get near hostile mobs.
rationale: Cheetah (level 20) is +30% speed, but any hit dazes you while it's on; swap to Hawk before a pull.

title: As a ghost, run straight
advice: Run straight to the corpse; mobs ignore ghosts and you can't be dazed.
rationale: Spirits run at 125% speed and nothing attacks them, so the shortest line is always right.

title: Use the guide's jump routes
advice: Follow the jump route exactly; one wrong drop is a death and a corpse run.
rationale: RestedXP includes mountain jump routes (e.g. the 'Deathless' Dun Morogh to Wetlands skip) that save long walks when done precisely.

title: Release right away
advice: Release now unless someone is about to resurrect you; every second dead is lost.
rationale: As a ghost you run at 125% speed; waiting at the corpse earns nothing. Decide corpse run vs spirit healer while you run.

title: Below 11: spirit res is (nearly) free
advice: At your level the spirit healer gives no sickness: resurrect there if the graveyard is closer to where you're going than your corpse is.
rationale: Resurrection sickness starts at level 11 (1 min, +1 per level, 10 min from 20). Spirit res still costs 25% durability in Classic; on the Forever beta we saw no durability loss from deaths below 10.
source: obs:data/live/*.jsonl (durability stayed 100% through deaths at levels 2-8; dropped from level 10)

title: Levels 11-19: short sickness
advice: Spirit res costs you (level - 10) minutes of 75% weaker stats; take it only if the corpse is farther than that and you'll spend the sickness travelling.
rationale: Sickness lasts 1 min at 11 up to 9 min at 19 and cuts stats and damage by 75%, plus 25% durability; a ghost covers ~525 yd per minute (125% of 7 yd/s).

title: 20+: corpse run almost always
advice: Run back to your corpse; spirit res at your level means 10 minutes at a quarter of your power.
rationale: From level 20 resurrection sickness lasts 10 minutes (-75% stats and damage) and spirit res costs 25% durability on top of the 10% from dying. Only take it if the next 10 minutes are pure travel or town work.

title: Spend sickness on non-combat work
advice: If you took the spirit res, spend the sickness on turn-ins, training, vendoring or flights, not fights.
rationale: Resurrection sickness only matters in combat; town errands during it lose nothing.

title: Resurrect away from the mobs
advice: Resurrect at the edge of the corpse range, away from what killed you, and eat before engaging.
rationale: You come back with low health and mana; reviving inside the camp usually means a second death.

title: Deathskip: die on purpose to travel
advice: Die near the graveyard the guide wants and take the spirit res: it's the fastest way to that town.
rationale: RestedXP's .deathskip steps (softcore only) use the spirit healer as a teleport; the cost is res sickness from level 11 and durability, which the guide accepts when the run back is long.

title: Hardcore: never deathskip
advice: You're on a hardcore character: skip this deathskip and walk or hearth.
rationale: RestedXP marks deathskips softcore-only; on hardcore a death ends the character.

title: Two deaths in 30 minutes: change the plan
advice: Two deaths recently: pull one at a time, eat to full before each pull, or skip this quest until you're a level higher.
rationale: Each death costs the corpse run (1-2 min) plus rest and repairs; the same pull pattern usually kills again. A level of difference changes hit, crit and resist rates noticeably.

title: Check durability after deaths
advice: Durability is getting low after these deaths; repair at the next vendor on the route.
rationale: Each death costs 10% durability on every equipped item and a spirit res 25% more; broken items give no stats.

title: Forever: low-level deaths may cost no durability
advice: Dying at your level appears to cost no durability on Forever, so a deathskip only costs the run.
rationale: Our recorder saw durability stay at 100% through several deaths at levels 2-8 on the beta, then drop from level 10. Classic charges 10% per death at all levels. Unverified on launch servers.
source: obs:data/live/*.jsonl (durability stayed 100% through deaths at levels 2-8; dropped from level 10)

title: Forever: check sickness after a deathskip
advice: After a spirit res, check your debuffs; if sickness shows up below 11, prefer corpse runs for deathskips.
rationale: RestedXP commented out some Forever deathskips because 'Resurrection Sickness is bugged' on the beta, and its code notes a spell cast on every Forever resurrection.

title: Low health in combat: decide now
advice: Low health: if the target is nearly dead, finish it; otherwise use your emergency button now, not at 5%.
rationale: Damage intake in a 1v1 at your level is roughly steady; at 30% you have a few seconds of decisions left. Potions, defensives and escapes all need a GCD or a cast window to work.

title: Low-health alert
advice: Health is low: finish the mob only if it's under ~20%; otherwise potion, defensive or disengage.
rationale: The low-health trigger fires at 30%; a mob at full health will outlast you, while one under 20% usually dies within two or three of your hits.

title: Drink a healing potion
advice: Drink a healing potion now if you carry one.
rationale: Healing potions share a 2-minute cooldown and heal instantly (Minor 70-90, Lesser 140-180, Healing 280-360); one potion is cheaper than a corpse run.

title: Finish a nearly dead target
advice: The target is almost dead: commit and finish it before healing.
rationale: A mob under 20% dies in a couple of hits; stopping to heal or run gives it free swings and can let humanoids flee for help.

title: Two or more on you and dropping
advice: Multiple mobs and half health: use your crowd control or escape now; kill the weakest only if it's nearly dead.
rationale: Two at-level mobs roughly double incoming damage; waiting until 25% leaves no time for a cast-time escape.

title: Skull mob: leave
advice: That target is far above you: back off and path around its aggro range.
rationale: Aggro radius grows ~1 yd per level the mob is above you (20 yd at equal level, up to 45 yd); a skull mob kills in a few hits and gives no more XP than a +4 mob.

title: Elite at your level: don't solo
advice: That's an elite near your level: skip it or get a group; most classes can't solo it safely.
rationale: Elites have roughly 2-3x the health and damage of normal mobs and give only 2x XP; hunters and warlocks with pets are the exception for low elites.

title: Target 3+ levels above
advice: Prefer mobs closer to your level: this one fights back much harder for only a little more XP.
rationale: Kill XP rises only 5% per level above you (max +20%), while each level of difference raises your miss and its crit/resist chances, so kills take longer and cost more health.

title: Gray mob: no XP
advice: That mob is gray: it gives no XP, so only kill it if it blocks the path or is a quest objective.
rationale: Gray level = level - floor(level/10) - 5 below 40 and level - floor(level/5) - 1 from 40; at or below it, kills give 0 XP.

title: Low green mob: little XP
advice: This mob is 5+ levels below you: it gives half the XP or less. Fine on the path, poor as a grind target.
rationale: XP = base * (1 - diff/ZD); ZD is 8 at 12-15, 11 at 20-29, 12 at 30-39, so -5 levels gives 38-58% of base.

title: Humanoids flee at low health
advice: Humanoids run at low health and bring friends: save a stun, snare or instant for the last 20%.
rationale: Many humanoids flee at about 15-20% health and pull nearby mobs back; a finisher held for that moment avoids a chase and an add.

title: This mob runs: control the end of the fight
advice: It's about to flee: keep a snare/stun or instant damage ready for when it turns.
rationale: A fleeing mob regains nothing but leads you into other mobs; killing it as it turns is the cheapest outcome.

title: Pull casters around a corner
advice: This mob is a caster: pull it, then step behind cover so it has to walk to you.
rationale: Breaking line of sight makes casters run into melee range instead of casting from range; for melee classes this removes 2-3 free casts per fight.

title: Interrupt the caster
advice: Interrupt or stun its first cast; casters do most of their damage with spells.
rationale: Interrupts (Kick, Pummel, Shield Bash, Earth Shock, Counterspell) lock a school for several seconds and shorten the fight.

title: Netting mob: don't plan to run
advice: This mob can net you: fight it where running isn't needed and kill it fast.
rationale: A net roots you for several seconds, so escaping is unreliable; RestedXP flags netters (e.g. Kolkar Wranglers, Prowlers) in its dangerous-mob notes.

title: Fearing mob: clear the area first
advice: This mob can fear you: clear nearby mobs first so the fear doesn't run you into a second pull.
rationale: Fear makes you run in a random direction for a few seconds; in a dense camp that usually adds a mob.

title: Healer: stop the heal
advice: It heals itself: interrupt or stun the heal, or burst it down below the heal threshold.
rationale: A self-heal near the end of the fight undoes several seconds of your damage; RestedXP notes mobs like the Murloc Forager that heal.

title: Enrages at low health
advice: It enrages near the end: save burst for the last 20-30% so it dies before the enrage matters.
rationale: Enrage effects raise the mob's attack speed or damage at low health (e.g. +20% attack speed under 20%).

title: Chargers hit hard on the opener
advice: This mob charges at range for a big hit: expect it on the pull, or pull it while it's already in melee range.
rationale: RestedXP notes boar Charge as a ranged-only opener dealing up to 40-100 damage at the boars' levels.

title: Give higher mobs a wider berth
advice: Path a little wider around mobs above your level; their aggro radius is bigger.
rationale: Aggro radius is ~20 yd at equal level and changes ~1 yd per level of difference (min ~5 yd, max 45 yd).

title: Don't turn your back on melee mobs
advice: You're in combat while travelling: kill it or keep facing it; running away invites a daze.
rationale: Each melee hit on your back has a daze chance (20% at equal level, up to 40%): -50% speed for 4 s, which lets the mob and its friends catch up.

title: Melee: pull with a ranged weapon
advice: Pull this caster with your throwing weapon or gun, then step back out of its line of sight.
rationale: A ranged pull plus LoS brings casters into melee; RestedXP buys warriors and rogues throwing weapons early for this.

title: After a death, single pulls
advice: Pull one mob at a time for the next few fights and start each at near-full health.
rationale: Deaths usually come from adds (patrols, social aggro, fleeing humanoids); single pulls at full health remove the variance at a small cost in speed.

title: Pull from the edge of packs
advice: Pull from the edge of the group; mobs standing close together often come as a pack.
rationale: Nearby mobs of the same kind assist each other (social aggro) within a few yards; murlocs, gnolls and kobold camps are classic two-for-one pulls.

title: Size pulls to your class and level
advice: Pull one at a time unless your class handles two: warriors with Sweeping Strikes (30+), AoE mages (22+), warlocks and hunters with a pet tanking.
rationale: Multi-pulls only pay when your damage scales with targets; otherwise two mobs take twice as long and do twice the damage, adding rest time.

title: Mobs reset if dragged too far
advice: If you have to run, run toward guards or back the way you came; mobs give up after a long chase.
rationale: Mobs evade back to their spawn after being pulled far enough; guards attack hostile mobs that follow you.

title: Melee: eat below half health
advice: Eat before the next pull; at this health an at-level mob can win.
rationale: A same-level mob deals roughly 40-60% of your health per fight; food restores it in 18-30 s (longer at higher food tiers), far less than a corpse run.

title: Enough health: pull
advice: You have enough health for one mob: pull now instead of sitting to full.
rationale: Sitting from 70% to 100% costs ~10 s of a 20-30 s eat; over an hour of single pulls that's minutes of XP.

title: Caster: drink before the next pull
advice: Drink now; starting a fight this low on mana forces a slow finish or a risky one.
rationale: Casters spend most of their mana per kill; the 5-second rule stops regen while casting, so a fight started dry ends with melee or a wand at a fraction of the damage.

title: Enough mana: pull
advice: You have enough for the next kill: pull instead of drinking to full.
rationale: Most at-level kills cost well under 50% mana; topping off from 65% wastes drink time.

title: Eat and drink together
advice: Low on both: eat and drink at the same time.
rationale: Food and drink run in parallel and both last the same 18-30 s; using them one after the other doubles the wait.

title: Health only: bandage instead of eating
advice: Use a bandage now instead of food; it heals faster and then eat only if you're still low.
rationale: A bandage channels for about 6-8 s and then 'Recently Bandaged' blocks another for 60 s; any damage interrupts it.

title: Buy the best food you can use
advice: Buy the highest-level food and water you can use; it restores more per second.
rationale: Food and drink scale with required level while the duration grows only from 18 s to 30 s; low-tier food at a higher level means longer or repeated sitting.

title: Five-second rule
advice: Finish with your wand or melee instead of another spell so mana regen restarts.
rationale: Spirit-based mana regen stops for 5 s after each spell cast; ending fights without casting lets regen run during the kill and the loot.

title: Restock food and water in towns
advice: Top up food (and water for mana users) to about two stacks while you're at a vendor.
rationale: Running out mid-loop forces either slow natural regen or a trip back; two stacks cover a typical loop.

title: Battle Shout before the pull
advice: Battle Shout.
rationale: Battle Shout costs 10 rage and lasts 2 minutes; casting it with leftover rage after a fight is free because rage decays out of combat. The player asked to be reminded only when it's missing and he has the rage.

title: Battle Shout after the first hits
advice: No rage for Battle Shout now; shout once Charge or the first hits give you 10 rage.
rationale: Rage starts at 0 out of combat; a Charge gives 9-15 rage depending on rank, enough to shout right after it.

title: Priest: Inner Fire
advice: Inner Fire.
rationale: Inner Fire (level 12) adds a large chunk of armor for 10 minutes; priests are hit in melee often while leveling.

title: Priest: Fortitude
advice: Power Word: Fortitude.
rationale: Extra Stamina is extra health per fight, fewer rest stops.

title: Druid: Mark of the Wild
advice: Mark of the Wild.
rationale: Mark adds armor, stats and resistances for 30 minutes; cast it before shifting since forms can't cast it.

title: Druid: Thorns before melee pulls
advice: Thorns before the pull.
rationale: Thorns (level 6) returns damage to every melee attacker for 10 minutes; at low levels it's a large share of your damage on multi-mob fights.

title: Shaman: Lightning Shield
advice: Lightning Shield before the pull.
rationale: Lightning Shield (level 8) deals damage each time a melee attacker hits you; worth its mana while you have it.

title: Mage: Arcane Intellect and armor
advice: Rebuff Arcane Intellect and your armor spell.
rationale: Arcane Intellect raises your mana pool (more casts per drink) and Frost/Ice Armor reduces melee damage and slows attackers.

title: Warlock: Demon Skin/Armor
advice: Demon Skin (Demon Armor from 20).
rationale: The warlock armor buff adds armor and health regen for 30 minutes; it cuts downtime for a class that heals by Drain Life.

title: Hunter: Aspect of the Hawk for fights
advice: Turn on Aspect of the Hawk before the pull.
rationale: Hawk (level 10) adds ranged attack power; hunters should fight in Hawk and travel in Cheetah.

title: Paladin: blessing up
advice: Blessing of Might (or Wisdom if you keep stopping to drink).
rationale: Might (level 4) adds attack power; Wisdom (level 14) adds mana per 5 s and cuts drinking for paladins who judge and heal a lot.

title: Forever: eat buff food before kill-heavy stretches
advice: If you have buff food, eat it for 10 s before this kill stretch; on Forever it adds kill XP for 15 minutes.
rationale: RestedXP's Forever guides state that any buff food grants 5% more experience from kills for 15 minutes (e.g. Herb Baked Egg). Classic buff food needs 10 s of eating to apply. Unverified by our recorder.

title: Warrior low health: buy time or leave
advice: Under 35%: if the mob is above 25%, use Intimidating Shout (22+) or Hamstring and walk off slow mobs; potion if you stay.
rationale: Warriors have no self-heal; their outs are fear (Intimidating Shout, 22), snare-and-run (Hamstring, 8), Retaliation for several melee attackers (20) and potions. Doing it at 35% leaves the GCDs to do it.

title: Open every pull with Charge
advice: Open with Charge: it closes the gap and gives you the rage to start.
rationale: Charge (level 4) generates 9 rage at rank 1 (12 and 15 at later ranks) and stuns briefly; without it a warrior starts every fight at 0 rage.

title: Rend only on mobs that will live
advice: Rend after Charge on a fresh at-level mob; skip it on anything that will die in a few hits.
rationale: Rend rank 1 is 10 rage for 15 damage over 9 s, better damage per rage than Heroic Strike rank 1 (15 rage, +11) but only if the mob lives the full duration.

title: Overpower after every dodge
advice: Overpower whenever it lights up after a dodge.
rationale: Overpower (level 12) costs 5 rage in Battle Stance, can't be dodged, blocked or parried and hits hard; it's the best damage per rage you have.

title: Execute under 20%
advice: Execute now.
rationale: Execute (level 24) works below 20% health and turns all remaining rage into damage, ending fights a swing or two early.

title: Heroic Strike only with spare rage
advice: You have spare rage: queue Heroic Strike (or Cleave on two mobs).
rationale: Heroic Strike replaces a white swing, which itself generates rage; it's efficient only when rage would otherwise cap or sit unused.

title: Bloodrage for an instant start
advice: Bloodrage now to get rage flowing.
rationale: Bloodrage (level 10) gives 10 rage at once and 10 more over 10 s for a little health; it fills the gap when Charge is down or you were pulled.

title: Hamstring fleeing humanoids
advice: Hamstring it before it runs.
rationale: Hamstring (level 8) slows the target; a slowed fleeing humanoid can't reach its friends.

title: Warrior weapon: slow two-hander
advice: For leveling, take the slowest, highest-damage two-hander you can use; weapon damage drives everything you do.
rationale: Charge-into-swing, Heroic Strike, Overpower, Mortal Strike and Whirlwind all scale with weapon damage, and big hits also generate more rage.

title: Arms at 30: pull two
advice: With Sweeping Strikes you can pull two mobs at a time; use it on doubled-up quest mobs.
rationale: Sweeping Strikes (Arms talent, available around 30) copies your next hits to a second target, so two mobs die in little more than the time of one.

title: Thunder Clap: skip for single pulls
advice: Don't spend rage or training money on Thunder Clap ranks unless you're fighting three or more at once.
rationale: Thunder Clap is weak against fewer than three targets for its rage cost; Icy Veins leaves it out of the leveling rotation entirely.

title: Warrior dual wield
advice: Dual wield is a Fury option from 20 in Classic; for leveling a slow two-hander is still the default.
rationale: Classic warriors learn Dual Wield at 20; RestedXP's item code allows off-hands from 18 on Forever (unverified).

title: Rogue low health: Evasion, Gouge, Sprint
advice: Evasion now (8+); if it's still going badly, Gouge and Sprint away, or Vanish (22+).
rationale: Evasion cuts incoming melee hits sharply for its duration; Gouge (6) incapacitates 4 s, Sprint (10) outruns most mobs, Vanish (22) drops combat. Blind (34) then bandage is the classic reset.

title: Train Dual Wield at 10
advice: Train Dual Wield at your trainer and put a weapon in your off hand right away.
rationale: Rogues learn Dual Wield at level 10; an off-hand weapon is a large damage increase for the cost of training.

title: Sinister Strike, then Eviscerate
advice: Sinister Strike to 3-4 combo points and Eviscerate; on a mob that will die anyway, don't build a fifth.
rationale: Overkill wastes energy: a 3-point Eviscerate on a mob at 30% is usually enough, and energy refills at 10 per second.

title: Slice and Dice for longer fights
advice: On a full-health or tough mob, open with a 1-2 point Slice and Dice, then build for Eviscerate.
rationale: Slice and Dice (level 10) speeds up white hits; it pays on fights that last its duration, not on quick kills.

title: Get poisons at 20
advice: Do the poison class quest at 20 and keep Instant Poison on your main hand from then on.
rationale: Poisons arrive through the level 20 class quest; poison procs add a large amount of damage to every fight.

title: Stealth past mobs you don't need
advice: Stealth through camps you don't need to clear; open with Cheap Shot or Garrote only on quest targets.
rationale: Stealth lets a rogue skip fights entirely, and openers from stealth start fights on your terms.

title: Swords for solo leveling
advice: For solo leveling, prefer a slow main-hand sword or mace with Sinister Strike; daggers shine in groups.
rationale: Sinister Strike scales with weapon damage; Backstab needs to be behind the target, which solo means only on openers.

title: Throw to pull casters
advice: Pull the caster with your throwing weapon and wait around a corner.
rationale: RestedXP equips rogues with throwing daggers; pulled casters that lose line of sight walk into melee.

title: Blind, then bandage
advice: Blind the mob and bandage; the bandage completes before Blind ends.
rationale: Blind (level 34, needs Blinding Powder) disorients for up to 10 s; a bandage channels about 8 s and breaks only on damage.

title: Mage low health: Nova and Blink
advice: Frost Nova, step away and finish with Frostbolt; Blink (20+) out if Nova is down. Polymorph a second mob.
rationale: Frost Nova (10) roots melee mobs; Blink (20) gives distance; Ice Barrier (talent) absorbs; a rooted mob can't hit you while you cast.

title: Conjure water before leaving town
advice: Conjure water (and food) while you're in town instead of buying it.
rationale: Conjure Water (level 4) and Food (6) cost only mana; mages never need to spend money on drinks.

title: Frostbolt, finish with wand or Fire Blast
advice: Frostbolt to slow and damage, Fire Blast or wand to finish; don't open a new cast on a nearly dead mob.
rationale: Frostbolt's slow keeps melee mobs from reaching you; finishing with an instant or wand stops wasted casts and starts mana regen sooner (5-second rule).

title: Polymorph the second mob
advice: Polymorph the add and kill the first mob.
rationale: Polymorph (level 8) takes a humanoid or beast out of the fight; two mobs on a mage double incoming damage.

title: AoE leveling from the low 20s
advice: If you're comfortable with it, the RestedXP AoE route (Blizzard, Frost Nova, Cone of Cold) is much faster from about 22.
rationale: Mages can pull 5+ mobs and kill them with Blizzard plus Improved Blizzard slows; Icy Veins puts the switch at 22 and RestedXP ships dedicated Forever AoE mage guides.

title: Evocation instead of drinking
advice: Use Evocation if it's ready instead of a full drink.
rationale: Evocation (level 20) restores about 60% of your mana over 8 s on a long cooldown; drinks take 18-30 s.

title: Wand early
advice: Get a wand as soon as you can (quest reward, vendor or an enchanter's Lesser Magic Wand).
rationale: Before 20 a wand is a big share of a mage's damage per mana; RestedXP routes early wand pickups.

title: Keep a mana gem
advice: Conjure a mana gem while in town; it's a free emergency mana potion.
rationale: Conjure Mana Agate arrives at 28; the gem restores mana instantly on its own cooldown.

title: Priest low health: Shield, Scream, heal
advice: Power Word: Shield, then a quick heal; Psychic Scream (14+) if there are two mobs.
rationale: PW:Shield absorbs the next hits and protects the heal cast from pushback; Psychic Scream (level 14) fears nearby enemies for a few seconds.

title: Shield, Pain, wand
advice: Shield if you'll take hits, Shadow Word: Pain, Mind Blast if mana allows, then wand it down.
rationale: A wand does most of a leveling priest's damage at no mana cost; spells set it up. Icy Veins: a significant amount of your damage comes from the wand.

title: Chain pulls during Spirit Tap
advice: Pull the next mob while Spirit Tap is up; you regenerate fast for a few seconds after each kill.
rationale: Spirit Tap (Shadow talent) doubles Spirit after killing an XP-giving mob, so back-to-back kills cut drinking.

title: Priest: wand upgrades first
advice: Treat a better wand as your top upgrade.
rationale: The wand is a priest's main damage source while leveling; spell power on gear is rare early.

title: Shadow at 40
advice: Plan for Shadowform at 40: it raises shadow damage and lowers physical damage taken.
rationale: Icy Veins' route: Discipline/Holy early for the wand, full Shadow at 40 for Shadowform and Mind Flay.

title: Heal with Renew while walking
advice: Cast Renew and walk to the next mob instead of eating.
rationale: A heal-over-time works while you move; sitting to eat costs 18-30 s.

title: Warlock low health: Fear, Drain, Healthstone
advice: Fear the mob (8+), use a Healthstone if you have one, then Drain Life; let the Voidwalker hold the rest.
rationale: Fear removes the attacker for a few seconds, a Healthstone heals instantly, and Drain Life heals while damaging; the Voidwalker can Sacrifice to shield you.

title: Voidwalker at 10
advice: Do the Voidwalker quest now and level with it out from here.
rationale: The Voidwalker tanks while your DoTs and wand kill; Icy Veins calls the Imp best 1-10, Voidwalker from 10.

title: DoTs, then wand
advice: Corruption and Curse of Agony, send the pet, then wand; don't spend mana on a mob the DoTs will kill.
rationale: Wand attacks cost no mana and let regen run after 5 s; DoTs provide most of the damage per mana.

title: Life Tap and Drain Life cycle
advice: Life Tap for mana instead of drinking, and heal it back with Drain Life on the next mob.
rationale: Life Tap converts health to mana; warlocks recover health while fighting via Drain Life, so the loop avoids sitting.

title: Stop runners with Curse of Recklessness
advice: On humanoids that run, Curse of Recklessness stops the flee (it does raise their attack power).
rationale: Classic Curse of Recklessness reduces armor, raises attack power and keeps the cursed target from fleeing.

title: Keep a few soul shards
advice: If you're low on shards, finish this mob with Drain Soul.
rationale: Shards come from Drain Soul kills and are spent on summoning the Voidwalker and on Healthstones; 3-4 in the bag covers a death and a stone.

title: Free mount at 40
advice: Don't save gold for a mount: your Felsteed comes from the level 40 class quest.
rationale: Warlocks and paladins get their level-40 mount through class quests without buying riding or a mount in Classic.

title: Hunter low health: let the pet tank
advice: Get the mob back on your pet (Growl), Wing Clip and step away; Feign Death (30+) drops aggro entirely.
rationale: Hunters survive by keeping mobs on the pet: Wing Clip (12) slows, Feign Death (30) clears threat, Mend Pet keeps the tank alive.

title: Tame a pet at 10
advice: Do the taming quests now; a pet is the hunter's tank and half the damage.
rationale: Hunters get pet access at 10 through a short quest chain; Beast Mastery leveling relies on the pet holding threat.

title: Mind the dead zone
advice: If the mob is on you, Wing Clip and step out past 8 yards, or let the pet take it.
rationale: Ranged shots don't work inside the dead zone (under ~8 yd); standing in it means melee-only damage.

title: Never run out of ammo
advice: Buy ammo here: keep at least several stacks, more before grind sections.
rationale: Out of ammo a hunter is a weak melee class; RestedXP asks for 10-15 stacks before its grindy sections.

title: Serpent Sting, auto shot, pet
advice: Send the pet, Serpent Sting, then Auto Shot; Arcane Shot only when mana is high.
rationale: Auto Shot is free damage; Arcane Shot is expensive and Icy Veins says to use it sparingly to cut downtime.

title: Keep the pet fed
advice: Buy food your pet eats and feed it when it isn't happy.
rationale: A happy pet deals more damage and gains loyalty; an unhappy one deals less and can eventually leave.

title: Feign Death to reset bad pulls
advice: Feign Death to drop the adds, then re-engage one at a time.
rationale: Feign Death (30) clears threat on everything; Icy Veins calls it one of the most important buttons a hunter has.

title: Paladin low health: bubble or heal
advice: Hammer of Justice (8+) and heal; Divine Protection/Shield if it's worse, Lay on Hands (10+) as the last resort.
rationale: Hammer of Justice stuns for a free heal cast; Divine Protection (6)/Divine Shield (34) make you immune; Lay on Hands (10) restores full health on a long cooldown.

title: Seal and judge
advice: Keep a seal up and judge when mana allows; auto-attack does the rest.
rationale: Icy Veins' leveling loop: auto-attack, Judgement on cooldown, re-seal; heal between mobs, not during.

title: Slow two-hander and Seal of Command
advice: Use the slowest strong two-hander; with Seal of Command (talent, ~20) slow weapons proc harder.
rationale: Seal of Command and Judgement scale with weapon damage; two-handers generally outperform one-handers for paladin leveling.

title: Exorcism on undead and demons
advice: Exorcism this target.
rationale: Exorcism (level 20) hits undead and demons hard; zones like Duskwood and the Plaguelands are full of them.

title: Paladin mana: Wisdom when drinking a lot
advice: If you're drinking after most fights, switch to Blessing of Wisdom and judge less.
rationale: Paladins regenerate mana slowly; Blessing of Wisdom (14) adds mana every 5 s and cuts drink stops.

title: Free warhorse at 40
advice: Don't save for a mount: your warhorse comes from the level 40 class quest.
rationale: Paladins and warlocks get their level-40 mount through class quests and don't need to buy riding or a mount.

title: Verigan's Fist quest (Alliance)
advice: The level-20 paladin chain ending in Verigan's Fist gives a strong two-handed hammer; do it if it fits the route.
rationale: Verigan's Fist is a well-known paladin class-quest two-hander for the 20s; weigh the chain's travel against your current weapon.

title: Shaman low health: heal or shock
advice: Earth Shock to interrupt or Frost Shock (20+) to slow, then Healing Wave; Reincarnation (30+) is the safety net.
rationale: Shamans can heal mid-fight; a shock buys the cast time. Reincarnation needs an Ankh and saves the corpse run.

title: Rockbiter early, Windfury at 30
advice: Keep Rockbiter on your weapon early; switch to Windfury Weapon at 30.
rationale: Icy Veins recommends Rockbiter as the consistent, mana-efficient early enchant; Windfury (30) adds burst on slow weapons.

title: Totem quests: Earth 4, Fire 10
advice: Do the totem quest when the guide routes it: totems are needed to cast that element's totem spells.
rationale: Shamans get the Earth, Fire, Water and Air totems from class quests at 4, 10, 20 and 30; Searing Totem (Fire) adds real damage early.

title: Two-handed weapons from 20
advice: Take the Enhancement talent for two-handed axes and maces at 20 and move to a slow two-hander.
rationale: Icy Veins: two-handers become usable at 20 via the Enhancement talent; slow weapons make Windfury and Stormstrike hit harder.

title: Lightning Bolt pull, then melee
advice: Pull with Lightning Bolt and melee as it arrives; keep mana for shocks and a heal.
rationale: One Bolt is free damage while the mob walks in; spending all mana on bolts leaves none for heals.

title: Carry an Ankh from 30
advice: Buy an Ankh or two for Reincarnation.
rationale: Reincarnation (level 30) revives you where you died without a corpse run; it needs an Ankh reagent.

title: Druid low health: shift and heal
advice: Bash (14+) or Entangling Roots, shift out, Regrowth or Healing Touch, then shift back.
rationale: Druids can heal mid-fight at the cost of a shift; a stun or root buys the cast. Bear Form's armor and health also reduce damage taken.

title: Bear Form at 10
advice: Do the Bear Form quest now; it's your biggest power spike.
rationale: Icy Veins calls Bear Form at 10 the largest power spike of druid leveling: mana-free damage and much better survival.

title: Cat Form at 20
advice: Train Cat Form and level in it for single targets: Claw or Rake for points, Rip or Ferocious Bite to finish.
rationale: Cat is faster for one mob; Icy Veins says to swap to Bear for several mobs at once.

title: Spend mana before shifting
advice: Open with Wrath or Moonfire while it walks in, then shift.
rationale: Mana regenerates while you're in form after the 5-second rule; spending it first is free damage.

title: Travel Form at 30
advice: Train Travel Form and use it for all outdoor runs.
rationale: Travel Form is +40% speed outdoors with no reagent, close to a mount ten levels early.

title: Aquatic Form for water quests
advice: The Aquatic Form quest at 16 pays off if your route has underwater objectives; otherwise it can wait.
rationale: Aquatic Form gives fast swimming and water breathing; RestedXP routes it when water quests follow.

title: Two mobs: Bear Form
advice: Two mobs: shift to Bear, Demoralizing Roar, and Swipe if you have it.
rationale: Bear takes less damage and its rage comes from being hit, which suits multiple attackers.

title: Melee: weapon upgrades come first
advice: For your class the weapon is the upgrade that matters: take the higher-damage weapon over armor.
rationale: Melee damage, and for warriors rage, come from weapon damage; a +20% DPS weapon speeds every kill, while a few points of armor barely change a fight.

title: Equip bag upgrades out of combat
advice: Equip the upgrade now while you're out of combat.
rationale: An upgrade left in the bag does nothing; equipping takes one click (weapons are swapped only out of combat).

title: Quest reward: upgrade, else vendor value
advice: Take the upgrade for your main stat or weapon; if nothing is an upgrade, take the one that sells for the most.
rationale: Quest rewards are free gear; a non-upgrade still converts to vendor gold toward training and the mount.

title: Under 10, don't chase armor
advice: Below level 10 armor upgrades barely matter; never detour for gear, only take what quests hand you.
rationale: Early mobs have little damage and fights last seconds; a weapon matters, an extra few armor does not.

title: Train the weapon type for a big upgrade
advice: If a big weapon upgrade is an untrained type, train it at a weapon master (10 silver) on your next capital visit.
rationale: Classic weapon masters teach any allowed weapon type for 10s (polearms 1g at 20). Alliance: Woo Ping in Stormwind, Buliwyf Stonehand/Bixi Wobblebonk in Ironforge, Ilyenia Moonfire in Darnassus; Horde: Sayoc/Hanashi in Orgrimmar, Ansekhwa in Thunder Bluff, Archibald in Undercity.

title: Fresh weapon skill: level it on easy mobs
advice: Your skill with this weapon is low: use it on low or even-level mobs until it catches up.
rationale: Max weapon skill is 5x level; below a mob's defense you miss more and land glancing blows. Skill gains are near 100% per swing while low, so it climbs quickly on easy targets.

title: Low skill in a dangerous area: keep the old weapon
advice: Fight here with your trained weapon and swap to the new one on easier mobs.
rationale: A weapon at very low skill misses often against at-level or higher mobs; the player made this call in Frostmane Hold on 2026-10-04 and it was right.

title: Can't equip: not trained
advice: If the game says you can't equip it, you lack that weapon skill; train it at a weapon master or pick another reward.
rationale: Warriors can't use staves until they train Staves; rogues can't dual wield before 10; the coach must check the trained skills list before suggesting a weapon.

title: Plate and mail: 40 in Classic, 35 per RestedXP Forever
advice: Warriors/paladins: plate; hunters/shamans: mail. Classic unlocks it at 40, RestedXP's Forever rules say 35: check your trainer.
rationale: In Classic the Plate Mail and Mail skills are trained at 40. RestedXP's item-upgrade code (and our gear module) allows them from 35 on Forever; not confirmed by Blizzard or our recorder.

title: Polearms
advice: Polearms need the Polearms skill: 1 gold at level 20 from Woo Ping (Stormwind) or Archibald (Undercity).
rationale: Classic polearm training requires level 20 and costs 1g; RestedXP's Forever item rules allow polearms from 18 (unverified).

title: Casters: wand, Intellect, Stamina
advice: Prefer a wand upgrade, then Intellect and Stamina; Spirit helps priests and mages between pulls.
rationale: Cloth casters level on wand damage and mana pool; Stamina keeps them alive when a mob reaches melee. RestedXP's stat weights for these classes rank Intellect/Stamina above armor.

title: Vendor weapons beat starter weapons
advice: If you still use a starter or quest-gray weapon, a vendor weapon of your level is a big, cheap upgrade.
rationale: Vendor whites at levels 5-15 cost silver and outdamage starter weapons noticeably; damage per swing drives melee kill speed.

title: Buy bags when money allows
advice: Buy a bag here if you still have a free bag slot; bag space is fewer vendor trips.
rationale: Every full-bag moment means destroying loot or walking to a vendor; a few silver for a 6-10 slot bag pays back in vendor gold alone.

title: Broken gear gives no stats
advice: Something is nearly broken: at 0 durability it gives no stats; repair before the next fights.
rationale: Broken items lose all their bonuses; for a weapon that means a huge damage loss.

title: Warriors and rogues: keep a ranged weapon
advice: Keep a throwing weapon or gun in the ranged slot for pulling casters and runners.
rationale: Throwing weapons need no ammo; RestedXP has warriors and rogues equip Balanced Throwing Daggers early.

title: Keep the Bag of Marbles
advice: If you have a Bag of Marbles, don't vendor it; RestedXP calls it useful all the way to 60.
rationale: RestedXP's Forever Elwynn guide warns not to vendor the Bag of Marbles reward from Gold Dust Exchange; its Forever effect isn't verified by us.

title: AH only when you're already in a capital
advice: List valuable green or blue BoE drops on the auction house only when you're already in a capital.
rationale: An AH detour costs minutes; a listing on the way is free gold toward the mount. On Forever's fresh economy, early prices for bags and BoEs are likely high (unverified).

title: Short on gold: train only what you use
advice: Train only the spells you press every fight; skip utility and situational ranks until gold is comfortable.
rationale: Training costs climb with level; RestedXP itself says to skip other spells to save money for later.

title: Train at even levels
advice: New spells are waiting at your trainer; train on your next town stop, not with a special trip.
rationale: Classic trainers add class spells every 2 levels; one visit per two levels on the route is enough.

title: Odd levels: no trainer trip
advice: Nothing new at the trainer this level; spend your talent point and keep going.
rationale: Classic class spells unlock at even levels (the player corrected the coach on this on 2026-10-04); talent points come every level from 10.

title: Save for the level 40 mount
advice: Start saving for your mount: sell everything, skip non-essential ranks, aim for 100 gold at 40.
rationale: Classic: riding costs 20g plus 80g for the mount (90g at Honored reputation). Forever folds the mount into the riding training and hasn't published the price, so plan on the Classic 100g.

title: Buy the mount now
advice: You can afford riding: go get the mount on your next capital stop.
rationale: A 60% speed mount cuts travel time by about 37%; with travel a large share of each hour, it's the biggest speed upgrade of the run.

title: Repair at vendors already on your route
advice: Repair at this stop; you're below 40% durability.
rationale: Repairs cost the same whenever you pay them; doing it at a vendor on the route avoids a special trip, and items at 0% give no stats.

title: Vendor on the route, not as a trip
advice: Sell gray items at this stop to free your bags.
rationale: Vendoring where you already stop costs seconds; a dedicated vendor trip costs minutes.

title: Mail gold early
advice: If gold is waiting on another character, mail it before you need it; cross-account mail can take up to an hour.
rationale: Mail between characters on different accounts is delayed; asking for it at 39 means waiting at 40.

title: Skinning on your own kills
advice: If you want gathering money, Skinning on mobs you already kill costs no route time; herbs and ore need detours.
rationale: Icy Veins' rogue guide recommends Skinning/Herbalism for income; speedrunners only gather what's on the path.

title: Keep cloth for bandages
advice: Keep the linen/wool you need for bandages; sell the rest.
rationale: Bandages cut downtime for every class; buying cloth back costs more than vendor value.

title: Don't buy leveling gear
advice: Don't spend mount money on leveling gear; quest rewards replace it within a few levels.
rationale: Gold at 40 is time saved for the rest of the run; a bought green is outleveled quickly.

title: Check money before training
advice: Sell first, then train the key spells; don't leave without your main damage rank.
rationale: Running short at the trainer either costs a return trip or a missing rank of your main attack.

title: Bags nearly full
advice: Bags nearly full: destroy the cheapest gray now if you're not near a vendor; sell at the next stop.
rationale: Quest items need a free slot; a full bag mid-objective costs kills you have to repeat.

title: No bag space while collecting
advice: Free a slot right now or the quest item won't loot.
rationale: With 0 slots, a quest drop stays on the corpse and can despawn; destroying a gray costs a few copper.

title: Low durability
advice: Durability is low: repair at the next vendor on the route before any risky pulls.
rationale: Each death costs 10% durability (spirit res another 25%); at 0% items stop giving stats.

title: Class reagents
advice: Check reagents here: Runes of Teleportation (mage), Ankhs (shaman), Flash Powder and Blinding Powder (rogue).
rationale: Reagent-based escapes and teleports fail silently when you're out, usually at the worst moment.

title: Don't vendor cooking ingredients
advice: Keep the meat and eggs the guide tells you to hold; you'll need them for Cooking later.
rationale: RestedXP keeps Boar Meat, Wolf Meat and Small Eggs to reach Cooking 10 and 50 for later quests; a recent RestedXP update added steps to preserve cooking ingredients.

title: Train First Aid
advice: Train First Aid at your next trainer town; bandages cut eating time for every class.
rationale: First Aid is a secondary profession (doesn't use a primary slot) and is cheap; bandages heal in ~6-8 s vs 18 s+ for food. Icy Veins recommends it immediately for warriors and rogues.

title: Craft bandages in dead time
advice: Craft bandages while you wait for the transport.
rationale: RestedXP repeatedly tells you to level First Aid while waiting for the tram, the Darkshore boat or the Menethil boat; the wait is otherwise idle.

title: Cooking 10 for a Darkshore quest
advice: Get Cooking to 10 before Darkshore; a quest in Auberdine needs it.
rationale: RestedXP: 'need 10 Cooking for a quest in Auberdine later'. Cook the boar and wolf meat you already loot.

title: Cooking 50 for a Duskwood quest
advice: Work Cooking toward 50 with the meat and eggs you loot; a Darkshire quest needs it.
rationale: RestedXP: 'need 50 Cooking for a quest in Duskwood later' and it keeps ingredients for it.

title: Sharpening/weight stones early
advice: If you have Blacksmithing or can buy them, use Rough Sharpening Stones (or Weightstones for blunt weapons).
rationale: RestedXP: Rough Sharpening Stones increase melee damage by 2; at low levels that's a large share of each hit.

title: Gather only what's on the path
advice: Pick up herbs or ore only when they're within a few steps of your line.
rationale: A 20-second detour per node adds up to minutes per hour; gathering on the line is free money.

title: End the session in an inn
advice: When you stop, log out in an inn or a capital: rest builds four times faster there.
rationale: Classic rest accrues 5% of a level per 8 hours in inns and capitals and a quarter of that elsewhere, up to 150% of a level. Logging out is also instant there.

title: Rested: do the kill-heavy steps now
advice: You're rested: kill quests and grinds pay double right now, so don't skip mobs on the path.
rationale: Rested doubles kill XP until the pool is spent (the pool counts the total kill XP, so a pool of R gives R/2 bonus); quest turn-ins don't use it.

title: Turn-ins don't use rested
advice: Quest and exploration XP don't touch your rested pool; only kills use it.
rationale: warcraft.wiki.gg: exploration and quest XP move the rest marker forward without consuming the reserve.

title: Grind gates are cheap while rested
advice: This grind goes twice as fast with your rested pool; good time to clear it.
rationale: Each kill pays double until the rested marker; a gate of N XP takes about half as many kills.

title: How much rest a break gives
advice: Eight hours logged out here gives 5% of a level in rest; it caps at one and a half levels after about 10 days.
rationale: Inn/capital: 5% of the current level's XP per 8 h (Classic); elsewhere a quarter of that; cap 150% of a level.

title: Long session: break while the hearth recharges
advice: If you need a break, take it now in this inn: rest builds and the hearth comes off cooldown meanwhile.
rationale: Cooldowns tick while logged out and inns accrue rest at the full rate; a break on the road earns a quarter rate and leaves the hearth idle.

title: Forever: camp tents give a slice of rest
advice: On Forever, sitting a minute at a campfire with a Camp Tent grants rest (reported up to 5% of a level) and then an hour of Boosted Rest; use one when it's on your path.
rationale: Community guides report the Leatherworking Camp Tent gives rested XP up to 5% of a level, followed by a 1-hour Boosted Rest debuff that blocks repeats. Unverified by our recorder.

title: Forever: Well Rested legacy perk
advice: If you have Legacy points, the Well Rested perk raises the rested cap and accrual; it suits session-based play.
rationale: WoW Forever's Legacy system (access around level 25) includes a Well Rested perk; Blizzard hasn't published the amount.

title: Pace benchmark for this level band
advice: Compare XP/hour with the band benchmark: ~14k under 10, ~17.5k in the teens, ~21k in the 20s, ~24.5k in the 30s, ~31.5k in the 40s, ~38.5k in the 50s.
rationale: The benchmark is ~70% of record pace (record splits: L20 in 6.5-8.5 h, L40 in 1d21h, L60 in 4d1h /played) and takes about 135 h /played for the 4,084,700 XP to 60.

title: Behind pace
advice: You're well behind pace: cut optional steps, stop full-resting, and check you're not stuck on a dry quest.
rationale: Below 60% of benchmark the usual culprits are long stalls on single steps, deaths, over-resting and detours; fixing the biggest one recovers most of the gap.

title: Far behind pace
advice: XP/hour is under half of benchmark: pick the biggest leak (deaths, wrong mob, waiting) and fix it now.
rationale: At 40% of benchmark a 10-hour band would take 25; it's never small inefficiencies at that point, it's a stall.

title: Ahead of pace
advice: You're ahead of benchmark; keep the same habits, don't add risky pulls to go faster.
rationale: Above 120% of a strong-run benchmark, the main risk to time is a death chain, not slowness.

title: Too long on one step
advice: Eight minutes on a travel or turn-in step: something's off; check the waypoint and the NPC location.
rationale: A turn-in or travel step should take one to three minutes on the guide's route.

title: Deaths are your biggest leak
advice: Three deaths this session: each cost about 2-3 minutes plus rest; play the next pulls safer.
rationale: A death costs the corpse run (1-2 min), resting to full, durability, and from 11 the sickness if you take the spirit healer.

title: Time to 60
advice: A strong RestedXP run is around 5-6 days /played; the record is just over 4 days; average players take 8-12 days.
rationale: Records: 4d1h17m (Vanilla Repack) and Joana's 4d20h; warcrafttavern puts typical players at 8-10 days and Wowhead around 12. Forever guides estimate ~150 h for an average player.

title: Split check on ding
advice: Split check: compare your /played with the benchmark: about 2 h at 10, 10 h at 20, 26 h at 30, 52 h at 40, 89 h at 50.
rationale: Cumulative /played at the benchmark XP/hour table (~70% of record pace); record splits are 1h12m at 10, 6h30m at 20, 16h46m at 30 and 4d1h at 60.

title: Long session: errors creep in
advice: Four hours in and dying again: take a break in an inn; tired play costs more than the break.
rationale: Late-session deaths and missed steps are a common pattern; a break in an inn also banks rest.

title: Recovering lost time
advice: To catch up: skip optional steps, stack objectives, eat only below half health, and grind gates on rested.
rationale: These four habits recover the largest share of lost time without adding risk.

title: About to ding
advice: You'll ding to an even level in a few minutes: plan to pass your trainer soon after.
rationale: Even levels bring new class spells; dinging right before a town stop saves a trip.

title: Spend the talent point
advice: Spend your talent point now.
rationale: Talent points come every level from 10; an unspent point is lost power until you notice.

title: Avoid respecs while leveling
advice: Pick one leveling build and stick with it; Classic respecs get more expensive each time.
rationale: The first respec is cheap but the price rises with each one; planned switches (AoE mage, Shadow priest at 40, Arms warrior at 30) are the exceptions.

title: Kill XP formula
advice: A same-level mob gives 5 x level + 45 XP; +5% per level above you (max +20%), less for lower mobs.
rationale: Classic (Azeroth): XP = 5*mob level+45 at equal level; higher mobs * (1+0.05*diff) capped at +4; lower mobs * (1 - diff/ZD).

title: The gray level
advice: Mobs at or below your gray level give nothing: below 40 that's level - floor(level/10) - 5, from 40 it's level - floor(level/5) - 1.
rationale: Examples: gray at 10 is 4, at 20 is 13, at 25 is 18, at 30 is 22, at 40 is 31, at 50 is 39, at 59 is 47.

title: Elites give double XP
advice: Elites give twice a normal mob's XP but usually take three or more times as long; only worth it in a group or for a quest.
rationale: Classic: elite XP = 2 x normal XP for the same level.

title: Group XP split
advice: In a group, kill XP is split: a duo gets half each, larger groups get a small bonus on top of the split.
rationale: Classic group modifiers: 1-2 players 1.0, 3 players 1.166, 4 players 1.3, 5 players 1.4, divided by group size.

title: Quest XP decay table
advice: Quests pay full XP up to 5 levels above their level, then 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% and finally 10% from 10 levels over.
rationale: Character level >= quest level + 10 gives 10% (rounded to 5); +6..+9 give 80/60/40/20%.

title: XP to 60
rationale: Classic XP table; the second half (50-60) alone is 1,778,600 XP, about 44% of the total.

title: Forever's early XP table matches Classic
advice: Your XP bar sizes match Classic: 400, 900, 1400, 2100, 2800, 3600, 4500, 5400, 6500 for levels 1-9.
rationale: Observed by our recorder on the Forever beta, along with level-1 kill XP matching the Classic formula exactly (Young Wolf 50, Kobold Vermin 52).
source: obs:knowledge/README.md (XP table 1-9 and level-1 kill XP match Classic on Forever)

title: Turn-ins will ding you
advice: Your completed quests are enough to level; turn them in before grinding any more.
rationale: Kill XP after the ding is no different, but the turn-ins may unlock the next quests and the trainer's new ranks.

title: Forever dungeons: quests carry the XP
advice: On Forever a dungeon pays through its quests: do one run per dungeon with every quest, don't chain-run it.
rationale: Blizzard cut dungeon kill XP and raised dungeon quest XP; the Oct 1 beta notes then cut the extra quest XP by 50%. Wailing Caverns' Deviate Hides went 1,600 (Classic) to ~4,650, then ~3,100 XP.

title: Don't farm dungeons for kill XP on Forever
advice: Second runs of the same dungeon are poor XP on Forever; go back to quests after the quest run.
rationale: Developer interview and guides: dungeon mob XP brought 'way down', designed to end chain-running instances to 60.

title: Quest while the group forms
advice: Keep questing or grinding near the entrance while you look for a group; don't stand at the portal.
rationale: RestedXP's Forever dungeon guide does exactly this (grind gnolls south of Sentinel Hill while assembling a Deadmines group).

title: Enter at the right level
advice: Enter when you're in the middle of the dungeon's range: quests then pay full XP and the mobs aren't orange.
rationale: Below the range the mobs out-level you; 5+ levels above the quests, turn-ins start losing XP (80% at +6).

title: Deadmines: skip Miners' Union Cards
advice: Skip the Miners' Union Card quest unless your group wants it: no dungeon bonus XP and it's slow.
rationale: RestedXP's Forever dungeon guide: this quest does not give the bonus XP of other dungeon quests and takes significantly longer.

title: Forever's early dungeons
advice: Forever adds Hall of Thanes (13-18) and Ruins of Lordaeron (15-20); RestedXP's dungeon route does them at 15-16 and 16-18, then Deadmines at 18-20.
rationale: Bracket levels from Forever guides; RestedXP's Forever dungeon guide chain: 15-16 Hall of Thanes, 16-18 Ruins of Lordaeron, 18-20 Deadmines.

title: Forever's later dungeons
advice: New Forever dungeons: Excavation Site: Wetlands (26-31), City of Dalaran (28-33), Drowned City (35-40), Krol'dok Stronghold (40-45), Alcaz Prison (48-53), Blackmaw Hold (55-60), Shaper's Terrace (58-60).
rationale: Excavation Site's 26-31 is from the Oct 1 beta notes; the other brackets come from Forever guide sites and may change.

title: Classic leveling dungeons by band
advice: Classic picks by band: Deadmines/Wailing Caverns high teens, SM in the 30s, Uldaman and Zul'Farrak in the 40s, Maraudon mid-40s, BRD from 52.
rationale: Wowhead's Classic basics list Uldaman 41+, Zul'Farrak 42+, Maraudon 46+, BRD 52+. On Forever, reduced kill XP means one quest run each, not repeats.

title: Healers and tanks find groups fastest
advice: As a healer/tank you'll fill a group in minutes, so dungeon quest runs cost you less waiting than DPS.
rationale: Group formation time is the hidden cost of a dungeon run; roles in short supply wait least.

title: Zephras Isle covers the first dozen levels
advice: Zephras Isle takes you from 1 to about 12-14; follow the guide off the island when it says, don't over-stay.
rationale: Community guides put the island at 1-12; RestedXP's Forever route runs '1-14 Zephras Isle' and sends Alliance next to Westfall (13-15).

title: Zephras: click windstone crystals
advice: Click the Windstone crystals you pass for free health and mana instead of sitting to eat.
rationale: RestedXP's Zephras route: 'Click Windstone crystals along the way for health and mana restoratives.'

title: Zephras: ride the tornadoes
advice: Touch a tornado before a long run: +40% movement for 5 minutes, but dealing damage ends it.
rationale: RestedXP Zephras text: approaching a tornado gives 40% increased movement speed for 5 minutes; dealing damage removes the effect.

title: Skyborne class options
advice: Skyborne can be Warrior, Hunter, Rogue or Druid on both sides; Mage only as High Order (Alliance), Shaman only as Windshaper (Horde).
rationale: From Forever race guides; Skyborne can't be Paladin, Priest or Warlock and requires the Skyborne pack.

title: Skyborne: glide down instead of walking around
advice: Use Walk on Air to glide off ledges and cliffs on your line instead of taking the path around.
rationale: Walk on Air is a 10 s glide on a ~2 min cooldown (beta race guides); it turns drops into shortcuts and prevents fall damage.

title: Skyborne: +5% vs elementals
advice: Elementals take 5% more damage from you: prefer them as grind targets when the choice is equal.
rationale: Skyborne racial Elemental Insight: damage to elementals +5% (race guides).

title: High Order: Read Ley Line while resting
advice: Use Read Ley Line before you sit: it doubles health and mana regeneration (15 minutes near a ley line, 15 s elsewhere).
rationale: High Order racial per Forever race guides: +100% health and mana regeneration. RestedXP removed its old ley line reminder, so its value away from ley lines is small.

title: Windshaper: Skysight for runs
advice: Use Skysight before long runs: +10% speed, mounted too (15 minutes near an elemental convergence).
rationale: Windshaper racial per Forever race guides; the long version needs an elemental convergence nearby.

title: The Great Outdoors: sit a full minute
advice: Type /sit by the campfire and stay seated a full minute until Boosted Rest appears; relog if it doesn't.
rationale: RestedXP Forever steps: /sit near the campfire, wait about 60 s for Camp Benefits and the Boosted Rest buff; 'If you don't receive the buff on the first try, log out and back in.' You can craft while sitting.

title: Camp Benefits don't stack with class buffs
advice: Camp object buffs last an hour but don't stack with matching class buffs; use them for what your party lacks.
rationale: Forever camping guides: sitting at a camp for 1 minute converts 'Campfire Nearby' into 'Camp Benefits'; buffs from objects are 1 hour and mutually exclusive with class buffs; campfires last ~10 minutes, 5-minute cooldown.

title: Camping 101 needs profession skill 20
advice: Camping 101 quests unlock a camp object for that profession once you reach skill 20; take only the ones for professions you actually have.
rationale: Forever guides: one Camping 101 quest per trained profession, learned at skill 20; RestedXP only accepts the ones matching your trained professions.

title: Forever: faster respawns in key zones
advice: Respawns here were sped up on Forever: you can usually finish kill and loot objectives by camping one spot.
rationale: Oct 1 beta notes: increased respawn rate across many creatures and objects in Hillsbrad Foothills, Ashenvale, Wetlands, Duskwood and Thousand Needles.

title: Forever routes differ from Classic
advice: Forever has over a thousand new quests; trust the RestedXP Forever route over Classic memory of a zone.
rationale: Blizzard announced 1,000+ new quests across 1-60; RestedXP's Forever guides differ from its Classic ones.

title: Forever mounts come with riding training
advice: On Forever, paying the riding trainer also gives you the mount; the price and level aren't published yet, so plan on Classic's 100 gold at 40.
rationale: Forever guides: a 'Burning Crusade-style' model where the mount is granted with the riding skill; no flying.

title: Beta values may change
advice: Anything Forever-specific I quote comes from the beta; Blizzard changed XP values as late as Oct 1, so treat it as provisional.
rationale: Oct 1 beta notes changed dungeon quest XP and respawns; launch is 2026-11-04.

title: Skyborne Horde leave by zeppelin
advice: When the guide finishes the island, take the zeppelin from Valanaar to Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.
rationale: Community beta guide: Valanaar has a zeppelin link to Mulgore; RestedXP recently reworked its Skyborne zeppelin route with waiting activities and departure safety notes.

title: 1-10: kill fast, don't rest much
advice: At these levels mobs die in seconds: pull the next one at half health or better.
rationale: Mobs at 1-9 have little health and damage; most deaths here come from 3+ mobs, not from low starting health.

title: 10-20: respect caster packs
advice: Teens: casters (Defias, gnoll mystics, kobold geomancers) do most of the damage; kill or interrupt them first.
rationale: Caster mobs out-damage melee mobs of the same level and sit at range; leaving them for last means taking their full cast cycle.

title: 20-30: elite quest mobs appear
