advice: Elite quest targets get common in the 20s; check the guide marks the quest before pulling.
rationale: From the 20s, zones like Redridge, Duskwood and Wetlands host elite areas; elites are ~2-3x a normal mob.

title: 30-40: dense high-damage zones
advice: This zone hits hard and mobs patrol: clear around your target before pulling and keep a cooldown for adds.
rationale: Mid-30s zones mix patrols, high-damage beasts and caster humanoids; most deaths come from adds, not the target.

title: 40s: mount and travel discipline
advice: In the 40s travel dominates: use the mount on every leg, fly long hops and keep hearths on the guide's plan.
rationale: Zones in the 40s are spread across both continents (Tanaris, Feralas, Hinterlands, Searing Gorge); RestedXP's Forever 40-50 route alternates them.

title: 50-60 is almost half the XP
advice: Levels 50-60 are 44% of all XP to 60: small per-pull savings here add up to hours.
rationale: 1,778,600 of 4,084,700 XP is earned from 50 to 60 (Classic table).

title: Session start checklist
advice: Before the first pull: check hearth bind and cooldown, free bag slots, durability and your self-buffs.
rationale: These four are the usual reasons a session stalls in its first 20 minutes (wrong hearth, full bags, broken gear, no buffs).

title: Quest abandoned
advice: If that abandon was a mistake, take the quest again now while you're near the giver; if the guide told you to, you'll pick it up again later.
rationale: RestedXP sometimes abandons on purpose ('Abandon ... You'll pick it up again'); an accidental abandon is cheapest to fix immediately.

title: Rebuff after it drops
advice: Recast the buff that dropped before the next pull.
rationale: Self-buffs are cheapest to refresh between fights; recasting mid-fight costs a GCD and resources.

title: Turn-in NPC missing: roleplay or escort
advice: If the NPC isn't at the marker, they're probably in a roleplay or escort: wait right there, it's usually under a minute.
rationale: RestedXP notes NPCs that move during roleplay sequences or leave for escorts and says to wait at the waypoint.

title: Shared spawns: kill everything
advice: If your target shares spawn points with other mobs, kill those too; it brings the target back faster.
rationale: RestedXP: 'its spawn is shared with other mob types, so kill everything to make them spawn faster.'

title: Deathskip lands at the nearest graveyard
advice: Make sure you die closer to the graveyard you want than to any other; the spirit healer you get is the nearest one.
rationale: You resurrect at the graveyard closest to where you died; RestedXP places deathskips where that's the target town (e.g. Kharanos from the Grizzled Den).

title: Whirlwind Axe chain at 30
advice: The level-30 Whirlwind Axe chain gives a big two-hander, but it's long and ends with an elite fight; do it only if your weapon is weak.
rationale: Icy Veins lists the Whirlwind Axe quest with the level 30 class quests; the time cost is the travel and the elite kill.

title: Berserker Stance quest at 30
advice: Berserker Stance (30 quest) matters for Whirlwind at 36 and Intercept; if you're Arms with Sweeping Strikes it can wait until the route passes it.
rationale: Icy Veins: Berserker Stance, Intercept and the Whirlwind Axe quest come at 30.

title: Redemption quest at 12
advice: The level 12 Redemption chain is optional for a solo speedrun; do it only when its steps are on your route.
rationale: A resurrection spell doesn't speed solo leveling; the chain costs travel.

title: Succubus and Felhunter are optional
advice: The Succubus (20) and Felhunter (30) quests are optional for solo leveling; the Voidwalker stays your leveling pet.
rationale: Icy Veins' leveling plan centres on the Voidwalker tanking while DoTs and wand do the damage.

title: Warlock 1-10: Imp and Shadow Bolt
advice: Let the Imp's Firebolt work; open with Shadow Bolt or Immolate and finish with melee or a wand.
rationale: Icy Veins: the Imp gives warlocks the best kill speed in the game from 1-10.

title: Hunter 1-9: shoot, then Raptor Strike
advice: Before the pet, open with shots and finish in melee with Raptor Strike; don't waste mana on Arcane Shot.
rationale: Hunters lack a tank before 10, so fights end in melee; mana is better saved for Serpent Sting on the next pull.

title: Priest 1-9: Smite, then wand
advice: Smite to pull, Shadow Word: Pain from 4, then melee or wand; shield before you get hit once you have it.
rationale: Early priests spend mana fast; Shadow Word: Pain plus wand/melee is the cheapest kill.

title: Druid 1-9: Wrath pull, then melee
advice: Wrath on the pull, Moonfire as it closes, then melee; heal between fights, not during.
rationale: Icy Veins: early druids level with Moonfire, Wrath and melee until Bear Form at 10.

title: Shaman 1-9: Rockbiter and melee
advice: Melee with Rockbiter up; Earth Shock interrupts casters and finishes runners.
rationale: Lightning Bolt spam drains a low-level shaman's mana; Rockbiter melee is mana-free damage.

title: Paladin 1-9: seal and swing
advice: Seal of Righteousness and auto-attack; keep mana for a heal instead of re-judging every fight.
rationale: Paladins regenerate mana slowly early; one heal saves a full eat break.

title: Mage 1-9: Frostbolt from 4
advice: Fireball until 4, then Frostbolt to slow the mob as it walks in; finish with melee or Fire Blast.
rationale: Frostbolt's slow means fewer melee hits taken, so fewer rest stops.

title: Two mobs: kill the dangerous one first
advice: Kill the caster or the lowest-health mob first; one fewer attacker halves incoming damage.
rationale: Damage taken scales with the number of attackers; focusing the quickest kill reduces the fight's total damage.

title: Use cooldowns at the start of a bad pull
advice: Three or more on you: use your crowd control and defensive cooldown now, not at 20% health.
rationale: A cooldown used early prevents more damage than the same cooldown used at the end of the fight.

title: Wait out the patrol
advice: This mob patrols: wait until it walks away from your target's camp before pulling.
rationale: RestedXP's dangerous-mob notes flag patrols (some fast, like the Elwynn lake murlocs) that 'can easily catch you off guard'.

title: Stunning mob: start at full health
advice: This mob stuns: top up before pulling it and never pull it with another mob.
rationale: Stuns remove your outs (potions, escapes) for their duration; RestedXP notes stunners such as Hogger ('Charge / Stun') and Ghouls (5 s stun).

title: Poison ticks block bandages
advice: Its poison keeps ticking after the fight and breaks bandages: eat, or cure it first if your class can.
rationale: Any damage, including damage over time, interrupts bandaging; druids, shamans and paladins can remove poison.

title: Health-regen debuffs
advice: Kill it fast: its debuff cuts all health regeneration by half for minutes.
rationale: RestedXP warns about mobs (e.g. Dire Wolves) whose Rabies reduces all health regen by 50% for 10 minutes; that doubles eat time.

title: Carry two or three healing potions
advice: Keep two or three healing potions; buy them here if this vendor sells them.
rationale: A potion (2-minute cooldown) turns a lost fight into a win; one saved death pays for a stack.

title: Use the scrolls you loot
advice: Use Scrolls of Strength, Agility, Stamina or Protection from drops on tough fights instead of vendoring them.
rationale: Scroll buffs last 30 minutes and cost nothing; their vendor value is a few copper.

title: Casters: Minor Wizard Oil early
advice: Minor Wizard Oil and Smoked Sagefish give a big early damage and regen boost if you can get them cheaply.
rationale: RestedXP: Minor Wizard Oil and Smoked Sagefish provide a high DPS increase in early levels.

title: Two primary professions only
advice: You can have two primary professions; First Aid, Cooking and Fishing don't count toward that limit.
rationale: Classic limits primary professions to two; secondary skills are free. RestedXP trains First Aid and Cooking for every class.

title: AoE dungeon groups on Forever
advice: AoE dungeon farming is weaker on Forever because dungeon kill XP was cut; use AoE on open-world packs instead.
rationale: Classic mage spell-cleave groups lived on dungeon kill XP; Forever reduced it (developer interview, guides).

title: New ranks waiting at the trainer
